headline: GTA 6 pre-orders confirmed for June 25 sending Take-Two up nearly 5%, while PLS drops 4.7% and the ASX had a rough Friday session, shedding 1.5%.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: GTA 6 pre-orders are officially opening June 25, with the full game launching in November. Rockstar also dropped official cover art. This is the biggest catalyst Take-Two has had in years — investors are betting the game will be a blockbuster, with some analysts expecting an $80 price point. The stock jumped nearly 5% last night.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG had a solid night, up 1.48%. A Seeking Alpha analysis highlighted that Google Cloud is outperforming both Microsoft Azure and AWS, and that Alphabet has a $462 billion cloud backlog — meaning customers have already committed to that much future spending. That's a massive runway for growth, and it's getting investors excited again.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a rough Friday session, falling 4.7% to $5.88. The lithium market remains in a supply surplus — there's simply more lithium being produced globally than the battery industry is currently consuming — and that's keeping prices depressed. News around Pilbara's Pilgangoora mine expansion is also raising debate about whether adding more supply is the right call in this environment.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 0.74% today, dragged down by broader weakness across the ASX and emerging market headwinds. The IEA's revised oil market outlook (factoring in the Iran conflict) is adding uncertainty to emerging market economies that are sensitive to energy prices.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped 0.56% today, largely reflecting the broader ASX 200 sell-off of 1.5%. As a diversified fund with heavy exposure to Australian and international shares, it tends to move with the market tide — nothing stock-specific here, just a soft day across the board.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL edged down 0.61% today. The IEA has warned that the Iran conflict is reshaping the global oil market outlook, with both supply and demand expected to contract in 2026. Oil itself (WTI crude) is sitting at $76.54 and barely moved, so it was more of a cautious day for energy stocks broadly.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.22% today — a quiet but positive session. The broader AI investment theme remains intact, with the G7 AI Summit dominating global headlines this week. No single catalyst today, just steady sentiment.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS was essentially flat today at +0.07%, closing at $525.46. It reflects last night's US session where markets were mostly calm — the S&P 500's last close was 7,420. US markets open tonight and could move VTS in the next session.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT was almost unchanged last night, up just 0.13% to $379.40. The stock is flagged as having earnings coming up, and analysts are watching closely. It's still down about 14% from your average buy price, so the earnings result will be a key moment to watch for a potential recovery.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 pre-orders open June 25 — big moment
watch_today.detail: Rockstar officially confirmed GTA 6 pre-orders kick off June 25, with a November launch. Cover art is out. One major shareholder is expecting an $80 price tag (vs the usual $70) and a third trailer when pre-orders go live. The stock jumped 4.93% last night and is now sitting in positive territory for your portfolio (+4.3%). This is the biggest near-term catalyst for the stock — watch how pre-order numbers are received.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium oversupply pain continues — down 4.7%
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell hard today to $5.88, and your position is now down 12.76% overall (-$19.14). The lithium hydroxide market is in surplus — too much supply, not enough demand — and there's no clear near-term catalyst to reverse this. The Pilgangoora expansion news is adding further debate. Unless you believe in a lithium price recovery in the next 12 months, this one needs a rethink.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Earnings on the horizon — watch closely
watch_today.detail: Microsoft barely moved last night (+0.13%), but the real story is that earnings are coming up and analysts are watching the Azure cloud growth story. You're currently down 14.4% on MSFT (-$57.38 AUD), so a strong earnings result could be the catalyst you need. A weak result could push it lower. Stay patient for now, but have a plan.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Google Cloud outperforming Azure and AWS
watch_today.detail: A detailed Seeking Alpha analysis out this week says Google Cloud is growing faster than both Microsoft Azure and Amazon AWS, with a $462 billion committed backlog. GOOG jumped 1.48% last night and your position is now up 19.5% overall. The AI spending theme and Berkshire Hathaway's reported interest are adding further tailwind. Looking solid.

watch_today.title: ASX 200 dropped 1.53% today — broad sell-off
watch_today.detail: The ASX 200 shed 137 points today to close at 8,828. This dragged down most of your ASX holdings (PLS, VGE, VDHG, FUEL). There's no single obvious catalyst in the data — likely a combination of global risk-off sentiment and the Iran/oil market uncertainty flagged by the IEA. US markets open tonight AEST and could set the tone for Monday.

watch_today.title: RBA holds interest rates — good news for borrowers
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia kept interest rates on hold at its latest meeting (decision published Friday). This is a relief for anyone with a mortgage or variable-rate loan — no more hikes for now. It also tends to be mildly positive for growth stocks and the broader market. The AUD/USD barely moved at 0.7016.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough Friday session, shedding 1.53% to close at 8,828 — a fairly broad sell-off with no single obvious driver, though global uncertainty around oil markets and the Iran situation is weighing on sentiment. Gold pulled back 1.2% to $4,172 USD/oz after a strong run. Oil (WTI crude) is nearly flat at $76.54. The Aussie dollar is steady at 70.16 US cents. US markets (S&P 500, NASDAQ) haven't opened yet tonight — last closes were S&P 7,420 and NASDAQ 26,021.

politics.summary: Two key domestic stories today: the RBA has left interest rates on hold — welcome relief for mortgage holders — and the Greens are blocking NDIS reforms in a budget standoff with the government.

stories.title: RBA leaves interest rates on hold
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia decided to leave interest rates unchanged at its latest meeting. For anyone with a mortgage or variable-rate debt, this means your repayments aren't going up again — at least not yet. It's also a mild positive for the share market, as lower-for-longer rates make growth stocks more attractive. The AUD held steady, suggesting traders weren't surprised by the call.

stories.title: NDIS reforms face delay as Greens play hardball on budget
stories.why_it_matters: The Greens are refusing to wave through the government's planned NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) reforms, using their Senate numbers to extract concessions in the broader budget negotiations. This means the reforms — which were designed to slow the growth of NDIS spending — are now delayed. For NDIS participants and carers, the current settings stay in place for now. For the budget bottom line, it adds uncertainty to the government's spending plans.

ai.summary: AI dominated the G7 summit agenda this week, with world leaders and Big Tech meeting to discuss who gets to set the rules for artificial intelligence. Regulation, geopolitics, and sustainability are the big themes — and for the first time, AI governance looks like a genuine geopolitical power struggle.

stories.title: G7 AI Summit 2026: Trump Meets Big Tech, AI Dominates The World?
stories.why_it_matters: World leaders at the G7 summit sat down with the heads of the biggest AI companies to work out how to govern artificial intelligence at a global level. The central question is whether AI ends up being regulated like a public utility — or whether the companies building it get to write the rules themselves. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOG, MSFT, and GXAI.AX, the outcome of these talks will shape what the industry looks like in 5 years.

stories.title: A Tale of Two AI Policy Regimes
stories.why_it_matters: Foreign Policy is reporting a clear split emerging between the US approach to AI (largely hands-off, let the companies innovate) and the EU approach (heavy regulation, rights-based framework). This divergence matters because it will determine where AI companies choose to build, hire, and deploy — and which governments end up with the most powerful AI infrastructure. US-listed AI stocks like GOOG and MSFT benefit from the lighter US regulatory touch.

stories.title: Get Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini in a single lifetime AI platform for under $70
stories.why_it_matters: A new bundled AI subscription is doing the rounds — offering lifetime access to Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), and Gemini (Google) in a single platform for under $70 USD. For everyday users, this is the most practical AI story of the week: instead of paying $20-30/month per service, you could lock in all three for a one-off fee. Worth a look if you're using AI tools regularly.

sport.summary: Big NRL Round 16 results today — the Titans pulled off a stunning 1-point win over the Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast, the Dolphins continued their red-hot form, and the Bulldogs snuck home against the Sea Eagles in golden point. AFL icon Tony Modra has provided a positive health update after a serious crash.

stories.title: Titans sneak past Panthers 19-18 at home
stories.why_it_matters: Your local team delivered on the Gold Coast today — the Titans beat the back-to-back premiers Penrith Panthers 19-18 at Cbus Super Stadium in what must have been a nervy finish. A one-point win over the Panthers is a big scalp. No text available on the full match details, but the scoreline tells the story.

stories.title: Dolphins make it 7 in a row, beat injury-hit Tigers 36-22
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins are on fire — seven wins in a row now after putting 36 past the Tigers at Campbelltown. The Tigers were reportedly hit hard by injury going into this one. Fox Sports described it as 'mission accomplished' for the Dolphins, who are now firmly in the top-eight conversation.

stories.title: Bulldogs sneak home against Sea Eagles in golden point 13-12
stories.why_it_matters: The Bulldogs edged the Sea Eagles 13-12 in golden point (that's the one-point extra-time try or field goal used to break a draw) at Accor Stadium. A tight one — Sea Eagles will be gutted to lose it so narrowly.

stories.title: Tony Modra stable and on the mend after major surgery
stories.why_it_matters: AFL icon Tony Modra — the former Adelaide Crows cult hero — is 'stable' and recovering after major surgery following what's been described as a harrowing crash. Multiple outlets reported widespread concern from the footy community. Fox Sports quoted those close to him saying 'everyone was concerned,' but the latest update is positive: he's got 'battle scars' but is on the mend. Good news for footy fans.
